ctx.x: So I started -- I put a band together there with a bunch of guys out here. There were a bunch of good guys out here then. There was, you know, Porfido, and Maini Charlie Kennedy and Joe Maney and -- a whole bunch of guys, guys that had been with me and other guys, and we rehearsed, and we played the Palladium and we played a season over in Catalina, and we'd play -- we were doing very nicely here, just playing weekends around L.A. And we never went -- and I would make a trip a year back east. I would go back --…

the couple of guys I'd brought with me, if any, and it was working out, except for one thing. You're doing nothing but maybe making a living and nothing constructive or creative, and I started to lose, frankly, to lose interest. And I'd do these things because it was a matter of money, and of course when my mother died -- I did that right up till '63, when my mother passed away. I came into quite a bit of money. And I didn't have to do anything, and I didn't do anything until about '66. Well, in '66 I started --…
